original_question: The Notebook asks whether every one-free-variable group formula is concise on residually finite groups: a finite set of satisfying elements should generate a finite subgroup. Conte and Petschick, Conciseness of first-order formulae, Question 1 and its preceding definition explicitly exclude parameters.
reviewed_claim: An actual parameter-free one-variable formula in the ordinary group language has exactly the two values central(1), central(-1) in the integral Heisenberg group; those values generate an infinite subgroup although the group is residually finite. The formula has prefix exists a,b; forall g,h; exists u,v and an equality-only conjunction.
checks: groupLanguage contains only identity of arity zero, inversion of arity one, and multiplication of arity two, with no relation symbols other than the equality supplied by first-order syntax. The structure interprets these as the given group operations. No Heisenberg element is added as a named parameter.

Formula Unit has one free-variable index. The actual bounded formula uses x as the free variable and six bound variables in the intended order. counterexampleFormula is real Mathlib syntax, not a semantic predicate disguised as a formula. realize_counterexampleFormula proves its interpretation for every group.

The algebraic FormulaCondition says x=[a,b] and every commutator [g,h] can be represented as [u,b]=[a,v], with [u,a]=[v,b]=1. The realization proof discharges the quantifier-order bridge; moving the x equation outside the universal block is legitimate because groups are inhabited.

H is the concrete Heisenberg group of integer triples with multiplication (r,s,t)(r2,s2,t2)=(r+r2,s+s2,t+t2+r*s2), the ordinary integral model. The residual-finiteness instance uses Mathlib Group.ResiduallyFinite and coordinate reduction to finite Heisenberg groups modulo abs(nonzero coordinate)+1.

formulaCondition_iff proves the entire value set is exactly the two displayed central elements. central_injective distinguishes them and the integer central embedding gives an injection of Z into their generated subgroup. Finiteness is of the whole formula-value set, and infinitude is of its actual ordinary Subgroup.closure.

NotebookStatement adds no nilpotency, finite-generation, torsion, or witness-specific assumptions. It universally quantifies over all residually finite groups and parameter-free formulas in the language. A Type-level concrete counterexample suffices to refute the mathematical universal claim.

The final negative theorem is closed; it uses the actual residual-finiteness instance and the syntax-to-semantics equality counterexample_values. It contains no oracle for the formula values or assumed representation of the generated subgroup.
scope_boundary: This disproves the full formula-conciseness question. It does not resolve the separate word-conciseness question 21.105. No claim is made here about every informal strengthening over all commutative coefficient rings.
